title: Adaptive Proximity Regularization for Inference-Time Alignment via Coverage-Aware Reward Hacking Mitigation
summary: This paper proposes an adaptive proximity regularization method for inference-time alignment that dynamically adjusts the strength of regularization based on the coverage of high-quality responses in the pre-trained policy. By analyzing the coverage properties of the policy, the method identifies regions where reward hacking is more likely and applies stronger regularization there. The approach combines coverage estimation with a modified MBR objective to balance reward optimization and proximity to the reference policy. Evaluation uses Best-of-N baselines with varying N on tasks from AlpacaFarm and Anthropic's hh-rlhf datasets, measuring both reward model scores and human preference metrics to demonstrate improved robustness against reward hacking.
gap: Existing inference-time alignment methods like MBR-BoN apply fixed regularization strength without considering the varying coverage of high-quality responses across prompts. While ref-004's InferenceTimePessimism rejects low-reward samples adaptively, it does not explicitly model coverage to adjust regularization strength. This leaves open the question of how to dynamically balance reward optimization and proximity based on coverage.
approach: The method estimates coverage as the fraction of samples exceeding a reward threshold (set at the 75th percentile of the reward distribution for the prompt). For low-coverage prompts (≤25%), MBR regularization weight α is set to 1.0; for high-coverage prompts (>25%), α is 0.5. The modified MBR objective is: argmax_y [E_{y'∼p(y|x)}[r(y',x)] + α·log p(y|x)], where r is the reward model, p(y|x) is the reference policy, and α is coverage-dependent. This differs from ref-003's fixed α=1.0 by introducing coverage-aware adaptation.
evaluation: Compared against Best-of-N (ref-003), MBR-BoN (ref-003), and InferenceTimePessimism (ref-004) on AlpacaFarm and hh-rlhf datasets. Metrics: (1) reward model score, (2) human preference ratings (from ref-003), (3) reward hacking rate measured as the fraction of responses with reward > threshold but human preference < 0.5. Ablation studies test fixed α=1.0 vs. coverage-aware α, and threshold settings (50th vs. 75th percentile).
